messages:
maria: Hey team, we've got a customer (acme-analytics) reporting a big p95/p99 latency spike since we onboarded model-id: hyper-llama-8k-v2 yesterday. p95 went from ~120ms to ~650ms on their long-context (6k tokens) workloads. They hit us via support ticket, attaching traces and a minimal repro.

sam: Thanks Maria. Any indication if it's server-side inference or tokenization time?

maria: The customer pasted a small client-side profile showing a big chunk in our /tokenize call — but their SDK is thin. They also sent a cURL repro:

maria: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"hyper-llama-8k-v2","input":"<~6k tokens prompt>"}'
```

kevin: Pinging the model onboarding notes — we upgraded tokenizer to bpe-v3 in the model bundle to fix a split bug. That tokenizer has a pure-Python fallback codepath if the C extension isn't present. If some hosts missed the compiled wheel, tokenization can explode CPU and latency.

oli: Confirmed on runtime: the rollout targeted mixed pool; a subset of hosts didn't get the wheel due to a packaging tag mismatch. Those hosts are hitting the slow fallback at 1k+ tokens and saturating the worker thread. I see increased sys CPU, and per-request tokenization time ~300ms for 500 tokens on affected nodes.

sam: Oof. Any quick mitigation we can do customer-side? Can we route them away from affected hosts?

oli: Yes. Short term: pin requests to nodes with the good wheel. We can add a routing rule to send traffic for model hyper-llama-8k-v2 to the healthy pool (node label: tokenizer:v3). I'll patch routing and bump nodes into the canary pool.

maria: I told the customer we'll throttle their long-context traffic to dedicated healthy nodes and follow up. They're okay with temporary slowdown on a/b tests but want an ETA.

kevin: Full fix: rebuild and publish the wheel with correct tags and push to the image; then restart the affected worker hosts so they pick it up. Also need a short test to detect fallback path on startup to avoid silent regressions.

oli: Working on an immediate script:

oli: ```bash
# detect fallback tokenizer presence
python -c "import tokenizer; print(tokenizer.using_c_ext())" || echo 'FALLBACK'
```

oli: I'll roll that check into the health probe and trigger node replacements for those reporting FALLBACK.

sam: Can you also add a temporary proxy-level mitigation? Maybe a header we can use to prefer older model variant until rollout complete?

kevin: We have hyper-llama-8k-v2 and hyper-llama-8k-v2-compat (older tokenizer) available. Add a routing rule that maps header `X-Model-Tokenizer: compat` to the compat variant. Customer can set that while we fix hosts.

maria: Customer accepted that. I'll send them the header and the short-term command to set it in their SDK.

maria: Also found one oddity in their traces: KV cache miss rate jumped after onboarding. Might be orthogonal but suspicious.

kevin: KV cache behavior can change with tokenization if token counts differ. If bpe-v3 splits differently, same prefix can hash to different token keys, causing misses and higher generation time. We should add an eval comparing token counts across tokenizer versions and warn customers on large-context workloads.

oli: Agreed. For now, the plan is:
- roll routing to healthy pool for hyper-llama-8k-v2 (15m)
- add header-based routing to hyper-llama-8k-v2-compat for customer (done, config pushed)
- rebuild/publish tokenizer wheel and restart affected nodes (ETA 2h)
- add startup health probe that detects fallback usage (PR in flight)

sam: I'll run a targeted synthetic test against 8k context to validate end-to-end after the node restarts. Want to confirm p95 back to baseline.

maria: Customer updated: applied header, they see p95 down to ~150ms for now. They're happy with the mitigation and want a postmortem.

kevin: I'll take postmortem write-up and include root cause (packaging tag mismatch -> missing C extension -> Python fallback), impact (p95/p99 spike for long-context requests on subset of hosts), and mitigations (routing, rebuild, health probe, tokenizer compatibility guide).

oli: Follow-up: created deploy-bot message during remediation:

deploy-bot: "Started rolling restart on nodes: node-42,node-47,node-51 — tokenizer wheel updated."

maria: Closing note to support: update KB with header workaround and add a checklist for onboarding tokenizers (verify C ext present, run long-context perf smoke).

sam: Thanks all. We should also add an alert when per-model tokenization p95 > 2x baseline to catch this earlier.

kevin: Agreed — I'll add that metric to the model health dashboard and assign playbook tasks.

maria: I'll file the customer postmortem ticket and drop a link here when ready. :thumbsup:
